app/src/views/components.js:3,11 — a view imports API_BASE from the data layer to build sprite URLs, coupling presentation to server configuration

churn_resistance.rationale: The boundaries are clean — one data module, pure view functions, shared templates for page and fragment — so a framework upgrade touches few files. The deductions are the hand-maintained static route list with a cwd-relative root and the env coupling leaked into a view.

findings.issue: Static assets are four hard-coded literal routes with serveStatic({ root: './public' }), which resolves against process.cwd(); adding an asset needs a source edit and starting the server from a different directory breaks assets entirely.
findings.suggestion: Serve the whole directory with one middleware — app.use('/assets/*', serveStatic({ root: pub })) — and resolve the root from import.meta.url (path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../public')) so it is cwd-independent.

findings.issue: apiJson's fetch has no timeout, so a hung upstream request hangs the page render forever and the cached promise never settles.
findings.suggestion: Pass { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) } to fetch; the existing p.catch(cache.delete) then clears the entry automatically.

findings.issue: A view template imports API_BASE from the data layer to construct sprite URLs, coupling presentation to server configuration.
findings.suggestion: Give pokemonCard a resolved sprite URL (or a mediaBase passed in with the data) so views stay pure functions of data.

findings.issue: onError returns a bare text body, dropping the page layout, and its (err, c) signature is the one signature Hono v5 changes.
findings.suggestion: Render the standard layout with a friendly error main; when upgrading to v5, switch to (c, next) and read c.error in one place.

findings.issue: The PokeAPI response shapes are completely untyped (typeLines: 0), so a data-shape change surfaces as scattered optional-chaining failures rather than at the boundary.
findings.suggestion: Add JSDoc @typedef declarations for the handful of API records (species, pokemon, type, generation) in api.js so the contract lives in one file and editors catch misuse.

summary: This is a lean, current-generation Hono app: the exact latest stable versions of hono, the node adapter and htmx, with data access isolated in one module and page/fragment rendering sharing the same templates. It already anticipates Hono v5 (separate adapter import, defensive query reads, ESM-only), so a major upgrade would touch a couple of lines. The remaining churn risks are a hand-listed, cwd-dependent static-asset setup, a missing fetch timeout, and zero typing on the API contract.
